A choropleth map shades each region by a value — emissions, population, votes, incidence. The
trick is always the same: join a table of values to a set of map shapes by a common key, then
pick a color scale. Here we build one in Python with
[canvasxpress](https://pypi.org/project/canvasxpress/): you pass one value per country and a
topoJSON of boundaries, and the join and coloring happen inside the render, so the result is
interactive and reproducible from a single spec.

## Install

```bash
pip install canvasxpress pandas
```

## One value per region

A choropleth needs exactly one measurement per shape. In canvasxpress the **columns** (`smps`)
are the regions — they match the map by name — and each **row** (`vars`) is a variable you can
color by. Here it's CO₂ emissions per country for 2018. We load a prepared table; swap it for
your own (any `country → value` table works).

```{python}
import pandas as pd

dat = pd.read_csv(
    "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-dat.txt",
    sep="\t", index_col=0,
)
smp = pd.read_csv(
    "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-smp.txt",
    sep="\t", index_col=0,
).reindex(dat.columns)        # align annotation to the country order

print(dat.shape)              # (1, N): one row (CO2) x N countries
dat.iloc[:, :4]
```

## Build the spec

`y` carries the matrix (`vars` = the variable, `smps` = the countries, `data` = the values); the
optional `x` block adds per-country annotations (continent, ISO code) for richer tooltips. The
country names in `smps` are what join to the map.

```{python}
from canvasxpress.canvas import CanvasXpress
from canvasxpress.render.jupyter import CXNoteBook
from IPython.display import display

data = {
    "y": {
        "vars": list(dat.index),            # ["CO2"]
        "smps": list(dat.columns),          # country names
        "data": dat.values.tolist(),        # [[values]]
    },
    "x": {
        "Continent": smp["Continent"].tolist(),
        "Code":      smp["Code"].tolist(),
    },
}

config = {
    "graphType": "Map",
    "colorBy":   "CO2",
    "topoJSON":  "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/maps/WORLD.json",
    "mapId":     "countries",
    "legendPosition": "left",
    "theme": "solarized",
    "title": "CO2 Emissions per Country (2018)",
}

cx = CanvasXpress(render_to="comap", data=data, config=config, width=700, height=500)
for part in CXNoteBook(cx).render():
    display(part)
```

Each country is shaded by its emissions, the legend maps color to value, and hovering a country
shows its name, continent and number. The whole figure is one portable spec you can store,
validate and re-render from R or JavaScript.

## Beyond the world map

Point `topoJSON` at a different boundary file to map US states, a single country's provinces, or
a custom region — the join key is just the shape name. Switch `colorBy` to a categorical column
for a qualitative map, add `decorations` to drop labeled markers on cities, or set
`mapProjection` for an Albers or Mercator view.
